title: How To Become A Better Teacher Instantly
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents a single, uncomfortable but transformational idea: taking full ownership of everything that happens in one's classroom, regardless of circumstances like a difficult principal, an unwanted grade level, or challenging students assigned by administration. He acknowledges that students remain responsible for their own behavior, but insists teachers should take responsibility anyway, because doing so shifts the teacher's internal state from victimhood to empowerment. The article describes concrete effects of this mental shift: reduced stress, an automatic search for solutions instead of complaints, and a more confident bearing that colleagues and administrators respect. He frames this ownership as true leadership, requiring the courage to stand alone and risk failure rather than lean on ready-made excuses. The piece closes with an extended metaphor of leaping off a ledge, urging readers to make the decision immediately, before the new school year begins.

quotes: It’s to take responsibility for everything that happens in your classroom. Ownership. Duty. Blame. Onus. The buck stops with me. The whole nine.
Take responsibility anyway. For it all. It can be the best teaching decision you’ve ever made. As soon as you do it, as soon as you say, “It’s on me,” things will instantly begin to change.
You’ll stop complaining and being a victim. You’ll instead automatically look for solutions. Your disposition and character will also change.

Taking responsibility is leadership. Not many people are willing to do it because it’s hard and takes toughness. You have to stand on your own two feet, embrace uncertainty, and risk the fear of excellence .
Do it now before the start of a new school year. It’s a decision, nothing more. Go on. Walk to the edge. Close your eyes. And take the leap.
